headline: 2 Bangladeshis killed, 4 in ICU after Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
summary: Bangladesh condemns the deadly assault on King Khalid International Airport and arranges to repatriate the bodies of the deceased at state expense.
details: Two Bangladeshi nationals were killed and four others are currently in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) following a deadly attack by Houthi rebels on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam confirmed the casualties during a briefing on Sunday, stating that the government is taking steps to repatriate the bodies of the deceased at state expense.
The Bangladesh government has strongly condemned the attack and called for an immediate end to the conflict and the protection of civilian lives.
The Bangladesh mission in Riyadh is coordinating with Saudi authorities to gather detailed information on the victims and provide necessary assistance to those affected.
The attack caused significant disruption to air travel, with multiple flights between Dhaka and Riyadh being cancelled due to the airport's closure.
State Minister Shama Obaid Islam urged Bangladeshis residing in Saudi Arabia to remain safe and noted that security situations at other Saudi airports are also being monitored.
caption:
Two Bangladeshis killed and four fighting for their lives in the ICU after a Houthi attack on Riyadh airport.

Two Bangladeshi nationals were killed and four others are currently in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) following a deadly attack by Houthi rebels on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaid Islam confirmed the casualties during a briefing on Sunday, stating that the government is taking steps to repatriate the bodies of the deceased at state expense.

The Bangladesh government has strongly condemned the attack and called for an immediate end to the conflict and the protection of civilian lives.

The Bangladesh mission in Riyadh is coordinating with Saudi authorities to gather detailed information on the victims and provide necessary assistance to those affected.

The attack caused significant disruption to air travel, with multiple flights between Dhaka and Riyadh being cancelled due to the airport's closure.

State Minister Shama Obaid Islam urged Bangladeshis residing in Saudi Arabia to remain safe and noted that security situations at other Saudi airports are also being monitored.

headline: 4 four people arrested for attempting to deface Tagore graffiti
summary: The suspects, including the President of Rashtra Sanglap Forum, were arrested in Dhaka for using black ink to erase a portrait of Rabindranath Tagore.
details: Four people have been arrested in a case filed over an alleged attempt to deface a graffiti of Rabindranath Tagore on a wall in front of the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy in Dhaka’s Segunbagicha.
The accused include ANM Ayas, President of the Rashtra Sanglap Forum, along with Md Sakibul Hasan, Md Sujon Mia, and Marzia Khandaker.
According to police, Ayas and others used black ink to deface the portrait of the legendary poet. Ayas was detained and subsequently taken to the police station.
The case was filed under sections 120B, 153A, and 295A of the Penal Code, relating to criminal conspiracy, promoting enmity between classes, and inciting religious hatred.
The graffiti was part of a series of portraits of 10 prominent figures who contributed to the country's art, literature, and culture, painted by the Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) on October 5.
These portraits included figures such as Rabindranath Tagore, national poet Kazi Nazrul Islam, artist Zainul Abedin, and filmmaker Satyajit Ray.
caption:
Four people arrested after attempting to erase a portrait of Rabindranath Tagore with black ink in Dhaka.

Four people have been arrested in a case filed over an alleged attempt to deface a graffiti of Rabindranath Tagore on a wall in front of the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy in Dhaka’s Segunbagicha.

The accused include ANM Ayas, President of the Rashtra Sanglap Forum, along with Md Sakibul Hasan, Md Sujon Mia, and Marzia Khandaker.

According to police, Ayas and others used black ink to deface the portrait of the legendary poet. Ayas was detained and subsequently taken to the police station.

The case was filed under sections 120B, 153A, and 295A of the Penal Code, relating to criminal conspiracy, promoting enmity between classes, and inciting religious hatred.

The graffiti was part of a series of portraits of 10 prominent figures who contributed to the country's art, literature, and culture, painted by the Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) on October 5.

These portraits included figures such as Rabindranath Tagore, national poet Kazi Nazrul Islam, artist Zainul Abedin, and filmmaker Satyajit Ray.
